{{Quote|He is a fencer. Leverage, position, advantage&mdash;they are as natural to him as breathing.|[[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn's]] [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] to [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] on [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], a Makashi master|<ref name="Yoda: Dark Rendezvous">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref>}}
'''Form II''', also known as '''Makashi''', '''The Way of the [[Ysalamiri/Legends|Ysalamiri]]''', or '''The Contention Form''', was the second of the seven classic forms of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. Developed for the purpose of lightsaber-to-lightsaber combat, to address the failings of [[Form I/Legends|Form I]], Makashi was the most dueling-centric of the seven classical forms. Relying on precision and efficiency over Shii-Cho's wild, sweeping motions, Form II allowed an initiate to defend themselves against an opponent with minimal effort, while placing a heavy focus on avoiding disarmament.

Makashi was described as elegant and focused, and was based on balance and footwork to outmaneuver opponents. Fluidity, precision, and economy of motion were relied on, rather than brute strength and brawn, with Form II bladework heavily utilizing jabs and light cuts instead of wild hack-and-slash movements. Overall, the form was at its fore when engaged in combat against a single enemy duelist. However, after the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] saw the destruction of most of the galaxy's Dark Jedi, the chances of a Jedi encountering a lightsaber-wielding opponent began to decrease drastically. In the intervening years, the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] and the [[Old Sith Wars]] began and ended in fits and starts, which caused the appearance of Dark Jedi and Sith to take on a sporadic pattern. This, combined with the increasing availability of blaster technology, resulted in Jedi encountering ever-increasing numbers of blaster wielding opponents, but only rarely encountering enemy duelists. As Makashi had been designed strictly for blade-to-blade combat, it lacked an effective means of combating enemies with projectile weapons. Due to this oversight, Makashi lost a great deal of its practical applicability, and over time it faded into relative obsolescence. It would eventually be supplanted by [[Form III/Legends|Form III]], which was both the most defensive of the seven forms and designed specifically for blast-deflection. However, the style would see a return to prominence during the New Sith Wars, a thousand years of off and on warfare which saw the rise and fall of numerous Sith organizations. After the Battle of Ruusan concluded these wars, the style once again faded from popular use and never regained any widespread practice amongst the Jedi.

==Description==
{{Quote|&hellip;a technique that helps one resist the Force attacks of an enemy, and is also excellent for lightsaber combat. It does more damage, but it leaves you vulnerable to other attacks. Use it against others wielding the Force or lightsabers, but not against anyone else.|[[Kreia]]|<ref name="Kotor II" />}}
[[File:KenobiVsVentress1.png|thumb|left|250px|Asajj Ventress utilizes her [[Jar'Kai/Legends|dual-blade]] practice of Makashi against Obi-Wan Kenobi's Soresu.]]
Of the seven forms, Makashi was the most akin to bladed weapon dueling, developed during an era where engagements with Darksiders and rogue Jedi became an almost routine activity. Form II's primary purpose was to serve as a counter to [[Form I/Legends|the first form, Shii-Cho]], by relying on precision swordplay to counter Form I's sweeping movements, with a heavy focus on preventing [[Sun djem/Legends|disarmament]], the primary goal of Form I.<ref name="Fightsaber" /> The early levels of Makashi were devised to provide a defense against an opponent's blade, allowing an initiate in the style to defend himself with minimal effort, but needing to be paired with a more offensive style to score a winning blow.<ref name="Street of Shadows">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref><ref name="SW.comFightsaber">{{SWArchive|url=games/videogames/news20080728.html|text=Fightsaber: Mastering the Art of Lightsaber Combat}}</ref>

The higher levels of the form proved considerably more effective. Form II bladework encouraged precision and efficiency over power, using jabs, parries and light cuts rather than slashes, blocks, and chops. The blade manipulation required for this form was very calculated, requiring intense focus and expert timing. It was described as elegant, powerful and precise, relying on feints to confuse and trap opponents. These refinements allowed a user of the form to attack and defend with minimal energy expenditure. Makashi also placed a great deal of emphasis on footwork in both attack and defense. The footwork of Form II practitioners commonly followed a single line, front and back, shifting the feet to keep in perfect balance as the practitioner advanced and retreated. Makashi was a style based on balance, on back-and-forth charges, thrusts, and sudden retreats. Makashi practitioners were also uncommonly adept at defending themselves from Force-based attacks. These elements combined to create a form that was extraordinarily effective for lightsaber combat against a single opponent.<ref name="Fightsaber" /><ref name="AOTCn">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="Kotor II" />

Form II emphasized fluid movement and anticipation of a weapon being swung at its target, and so required very smooth motion of both the blade and the body, and practitioners often wielded the blade one-handed for a greater range of movement. With a skilled practitioner, the results were deadly. In fact, masters of the form often seemed so relaxed when employing it that they appeared to be dancing.<ref name="AOTCn" /> Makashi duelists also trained themselves to avoid enslavement to form, as such devotion opened the practitioner to be defeated by unpredictable tactics — what [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] dubbed "the unforeseen".<ref name="LoE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>

[[File:Dooku_Open_Seasons.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Dooku deflects blaster bolts.]]
However, for all its effectiveness, Form II was not without its weaknesses. As it was designed to combat enemy duelists rather than enemy gunmen, it provided poor blast-deflection training. While this was ultimately the reason for the style's decline and eventual obsolescence, it could be overcome through skill and practice.<ref name="RotSn">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Also, Makashi was most potent when used against a single opponent, and was reduced in effectiveness when fighting groups of adversaries. However, skilled practitioners could still fare very well against multiple foes;<ref name="SW.comFightsaber" /> Dooku could engage up to three opponents with little difficulty, relying on his footwork to outmaneuver them and take them one at a time;<ref name="RotSn" /><ref name="Nightsisters">{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}}</ref> [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] compensated by [[Jar'Kai/Legends|wielding dual-blades]].<ref name="Cloak of Darkness">{{TCW|Cloak of Darkness}}</ref><ref name="Massacre">{{TCW|Massacre}}</ref>

However, the greatest flaw of the Makashi system of combat was its inability to generate kinetic energy in its application; the focus on precision and blade control hampered an adherent's ability to generate momentum in both offensive and defensive maneuvers. This meant that a duelist who possessed a sufficient level of physical strength could potentially overwhelm a Makashi practitioner, shunting aside strikes from the form's precision offense and simply bashing through its evasive, footwork-oriented defense. This lack of physical force left Makashi practitioners vulnerable to duelists utilizing more contemporary forms, which emphasized power and brute strength. This weakness was especially pronounced against practitioners of the Djem So variant of [[Form V/Legends|Form V]], as the style was based almost entirely around fast, strength-oriented swordplay.<ref name="RotSn" /> However, this weakness could, to varying degrees, be compensated for with rigorous strength training or cybernetic augmentation.<ref name="TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /> Additionally, as demonstrated by Dooku's numerous victories against power duelists during the Clone Wars, simply utilizing a strength-oriented style against a Makashi practitioner was no guarantee of victory.<ref name="AOTCn" />

===Known moves and maneuvers===
{{Quote|Masters of Form II develop unique offenses and defenses, and trained studiously against having their weapon taken or damaged.|Cin Drallig on Form II|<ref name="EGTTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
[[File:MakashiMovesManeuversTJP.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Jedi duelist performs the Makashi salute prior to engaging an opponent.]]
Being a style geared towards efficiency, Makashi adherents relied on balance and economy of movement, preferring to refrain from the leaps and acrobatics common to [[Form IV/Legends|Form IV]].<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> The Form II opening stance was a single handed low guard. The saber would be held in the strong hand of the user, and held at their side, the blade pointed down, and the feet would be shoulder width apart. Some faced their opponent side on, so the blade was pointed in their direction. The lightsaber hilt would be held with the thumb pointing down the length of the blade to allow for smaller, tighter, more accurate movements of the saber. The rest of the fingers wrap around the hilt holding it tightly, but not so tight as to limit the fluidity of the movements. The typical Makashi flourish consisted of rapidly moving the tip of the blade in an X shaped pattern through the air, often following the Makashi salute. The salute was not an attack or maneuver but a challenge to an opponent. The saber was held in one hand, brought up vertical directly in front of the practitioner's face, then swung down in a Makashi flourish.<ref name="LoE" />

Makashi duelists were typically skilled in the application of two [[Lightsaber combat/Legends#Marks of Contact|Marks of Contact]]; the ''[[Sun djem/Legends|Sun djem]]'' and the ''[[Shiak]]''. In a marked difference from the Shii-Cho "disarming slash" maneuver, which was a power attack designed to rip an opponents weapon from their grasp, the typical Form II applications of the ''sun djem'' were precise attacks directed at the weapon itself, often destroying it or even burning through an opponents fingers to disarm them. Applications of the ''shiak'' were a natural result of Form II footwork and swordplay, all of which followed a single back and forth line, and was seen as an indication of skill and control.<ref name="TJP" /> Two Makashi maneuvers were the "contentious opportunity" and the "Makashi riposte". The "contentious opportunity" was based around recognizing and exploiting an opening in the opponent's defense before swiftly moving to strike the exposed enemy. The "Makashi riposte" was similarly designed to slightly alter the angle of an opponent's attack before quickly retaliating with a counter strike.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>

===Makashi Weapon Specifications===
{{Quote|The curved-hilt lightsaber is perhaps the least radical of all variants. Its extended handle accommodates a slight bend seldom exceeding thirty degrees. This style is common among practitioners of Form II lightsaber combat, who prefer its balanced weight and precise handling for saber-to-saber dueling.|[[Skarch Vaunk]] in [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]|<ref name="TJP" />}}
[[File:DookuSaber-MR.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus's]] curved-hilt lightsaber]]
Due to Form II's emphasis on blade manipulation, and its many fluid one-handed moves, Makashi practitioners often wielded lightsabers that were specialized for such use. The most prominent weapon for this purpose was the [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved-hilt lightsaber]]. These weapons were used because the curved hilt fit better into the palm, granting better blade control and allowing for greater precision and strength.<ref name="PoD" /> In addition to this, wielders often created highly decorated weapons, and occasionally included blade-guards, as shown with [[Dooku's lightsaber/Legends|Dooku's lightsaber]].<ref name="AOTCvd">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

The other, considerably rarer, weapon type was the [[Lightfoil/Legends|Lightfoil]], a specialized type of lightsaber used by the [[Mecrosa Order]]. Original lightfoils were built with small handles for exclusively one-handed usage, and were much better balanced than typical lightsabers, allowing for greater precision.<ref name="JATM" /> However, curved lightsabers and lightfoils were not the only weapons that Makashi could be effectively utilized with; [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]],<ref name="CW Adventures">[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Adventures'' video game]]</ref> [[Kento Marek]], and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] all wielded lightsaber with standard hilts,<ref name="TFUn" /> and Asajj Ventress demonstrated the ability to utilize the style with a [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|saberstaff]].<ref name="TCWf">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref>

==Applications==
{{Quote|Finesse. Artfulness. Economy.|Darth Tyranus|<ref name="LoE" />}}
[[File:YodaTyranusduel.png|thumb|left|250px|Dooku utilizes Makashi against Yoda's Form IV mastery.]]
Count Dooku, alias Darth Tyranus, was one of the finest practitioners of Makashi in his day, mastering the form at its highest levels. He personally emphasized emotional levelheadedness and tactical know-how over the rage-fueled frenzy many of his opponents, including Anakin Skywalker, and even some of his students, relied on, examples including [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] or [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]].<ref name="LoE" /> He demonstrated precision and elegance in his bladework, with a pin-point accurate and unpredictable offense reinforced by an almost effortless defense, all drilled and practiced to the point of being instinct.<ref name="RotSn" /><ref name="AOTCn" /> He relied on feints to entrap his opponents, and footwork to outmaneuver, basing himself around balance and mobility. Dooku would use these skills to work his way around opponents, deflecting and evading their attacks rather than trying to meet them head-to-head. His skill with the style marked him out as one of the greatest swordmasters produced by the Jedi Order, and the Form's rarity provided him with an edge against most duelists, who simply were not prepared for the finesse and precise movements of a form bred for lightsaber dueling.<ref name="AOTCn" /> The sole dedication to Makashi Dooku emphasised into his lightsaber training managed to grant him knowledge and skill nigh-unrivalled by any other Force sensitive during his time, truly showcasing how the exactness and fluent efficiency of a genuine Form II master made for a highly formidable duelist.

[[File:DookuVSGrievous.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Dooku uses Makashi in a sparring match with Grievous.]]
Dooku's practical application of the form was exemplary; his skills were surpassed only by [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], and only [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] was credited as Dooku's equal.<ref name="Yoda: Dark Rendezvous" /> On Geonosis, he [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|demonstrated]] many of these skills against [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. His efficient defensive maneuvers left the Jedi's [[Form III/Legends|swift slashes]] looking exaggerated and overdone, while Kenobi struggled to catch up to the Count's precise ripostes and unpredictable feints. During their initial duel, many of Kenobi's parries and blocks missed Dooku's blade completely, forcing him to retreat. Kenobi was ultimately brought down by light, though damaging cuts across his left arm and thigh.<ref name="AOTCn" />

However, despite Tyranus' absolute mastery of Form II, he was still prone to one of the style's weaknesses; the lack of kinetic power. Perhaps the most notable demonstration of this was during Tyranus' fateful duel with Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi; he was simply unable to generate the necessary power to evenly match Skywalker's preferred form, [[Form V|Djem So]], nor to penetrate the defenses of Kenobi's [[Form III]]. The sheer, raw power of Form V wore down Tyranus' defenses, physically exhausting him and draining his reserves of [[The Force|Force power]]. This weakness, combined with his age and Skywalker's overwhelming skill and power, resulted in his defeat.<ref name="RotSn" /> Earlier on, Tyranus had been disarmed by [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], a towering juggernaut who received little lightsaber training.<ref name="Witches of the Mist">{{TCW|Witches of the Mist}}</ref>

[[File:Tranquility_detention_blocks.png|thumb|left|250px|Asajj Ventress engages Luminara Unduli and Ahsoka Tano.]]
Another Form II practitioner active at this time was Asajj Ventress, Tyranus' best assassin.<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /> Developing her skills under Tyranus' tutelage, her eventual prowess as a duelist enabled her to hold her own against up to three adversaries with little difficulty, demonstrated during her [[Mission to Ruul (Clone Wars)|mission]] to [[Ruul (moon)|Ruul]].<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu">''[[Jedi: Mace Windu]]''</ref> Her skills even advanced to the point where she was able to defeat Kit Fisto,<ref name="The Cestus Deception">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref> disarm Obi-Wan Kenobi,<ref name="TCWf" /> and hold her own against Mace Windu,<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" /><ref name="Fashion">{{TCWComicCite|6.23|Fashion}}</ref> all three of whom were [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] members.

However, Ventress was no master, and while she demonstrated both elegant bladework and sophisticated footwork,<ref name="Yoda: Dark Rendezvous" /> her form lacked refinement.<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /> Rather than practice emotional levelheadedness as Dooku did, she often grew impassioned and fought with animal rage.<ref name="LoE" /><ref name="CWvd">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> While this angry onslaught enabled her to engage, and even defeat, some of the best Jedi duelists of her day,<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /><ref name="The Cestus Deception" /> [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] believed it could also compromise her tactical planning abilities.<ref name="EGTTF" />

During her earlier years, she lacked the physical strength necessary to compensate for the inherent weaknesses of both Makashi and dual-blade combat. Her attacks lacked power, as shown by both Dooku's casual defensive moves during their bout on Rattatak,<ref name="CWC7">{{CW|7}}</ref> and her retreat before Anakin Skywalker's frenzy of power attacks during [[Duel on Yavin 4|their duel on Yavin 4]].<ref name="CWC19">{{CW|19}}</ref> However, she eventually developed the strength necessary to compensate for this weakness, demonstrating the ability to hold up simultaneous bladelocks with multiple duelists at a time;<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /> she could even manage to hold off the strikes of physically superior opponents such as General Grievous or Savage Opress, if only temporarily.<ref name="Massacre" /><ref name="Revenge">{{TCW|Revenge (episode)}}</ref> Ventress was initially heavily reliant on her extra blade, and was left at a disadvantage if deprived of it,<ref name="TCWf" /> though she eventually overcame this with time.<ref name="TCW 9">[[The Clone Wars 9|''The Clone Wars'' 9]]</ref>

==Practitioners==
{{Quote|Even with my vision clouded, I recognize the fighting style of Count Dooku.|[[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]] analyzing Asajj Ventress' bladework|<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" />}}
[[File:Seperatist_leadership.jpg|thumb|300px|Dooku trained both Grievous and Asajj Ventress in Makashi.]]
Form II's primary niche was among Jedi duelists who engaged Darksiders, or conversely, Darksiders who engaged Jedi. Examples of such combatants include [[Kreia]], who later taught the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] the basics of the form;<ref name="Kotor II" /> [[Rance Lussk]], the top student at the [[Odacer-Faustin Sith academy|Sith academy]] on [[Odacer-Faustin]]<ref name="RH">[[Red Harvest (novel)|''Red Harvest'']]</ref> or the Sith apprentice [[Fohargh]], who was trained by the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith Blademaster|Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]].<ref name="PoD" /> However, following the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|final battle of Ruusan]], Makashi was left obsolete; the dueling-centric form lacked proper blast-deflect techniques to make it a practical fighting method against criminals, and the number of active lightsaber-wielding Darksiders to engage was practically nil.<ref name="EGTTF" /> Nevertheless, Form II was still taught among the Jedi, with proponents such as [[Skarch Vaunk]] praising the mental discipline it instilled. In fact, the Jedi-held Mid-Year Fete featured classical Makashi duels between the various participating swordmasters, ensuring the style's continued survival and use. Furthermore, the attitude towards the style's obsolescence was disputed by notables such as Obi-Wan Kenobi, who argued that the idea that there were no enemy lightsaber duelists to combat was mere wishful thinking.<ref name="TJP" />

Despite this, by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], few practiced the form, the most notable being Dooku.<ref name="Fightsaber" /> Like Skarch Vaunk, Dooku argued Makashi's continuing relevance was due to the discipline it instilled, and held it among the highest of fighting forms.<ref name="AOTCn" /> Other Jedi practitioners of Makashi included Dooku's former Padawan Qui-Gon Jinn;<ref name="Lightsabers">''[[Star Wars: Lightsabers: A Guide to Weapons of the Force]]''</ref> famed [[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemaster]] [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]];<ref name="EGTTF" /> Jedi Council [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] Shaak Ti;<ref name="CW Adventures" /> and Master [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]], who was said to have mastered the form.<ref name="Official Starships & Vehicles 27">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 27|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 27]]</ref> [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] Yoda appeared to have also used the form, as he had once taught Dooku the Makashi salute.<ref name="AOTC junior novel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones'' junior novelization]]</ref> As Darth Tyranus, Dooku trained both Asajj Ventress and Grievous in Form II.<ref name="RotSn" /><ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /> Makashi evidently became one of Grievous' primary fighting methods, as many of his opponents commented on Dooku's influence in his technique, and he passed this training on to his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]].<ref name="LoE" />

[[File:Nautolan_Fem_Sith_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A [[Unidentified Nautolan darksider|Nautolan darksider]] in the opening stance of Form II]]
During the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] Darth Vader studied and mastered Form II and he often incorporated many elements of Makashi into his personalized Djem So variant, taking advantage of his cybernetically augmented strength to overcome Makashi's prime weakness.<ref name="TFUn" /> His proficiency even proved great enough to having managed to develop an unorthodox form of Makashi, in which he would rely on the great precision and economy of movement his study of the form granted him by wielding it one-handed but also retaining great power: a method that he applied effectively against [[Olee Starstone]] and his own son [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], swiftly besting the former and briefly overwhelming Luke.<ref name="RoDV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref><ref name="Episode V">{{Film|V}}</ref>

The Jedi Knight Kento Marek also included elements of Makashi in his bladework, though his understanding of the style was limited. Vader's apprentice, [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]], was versed enough in Form II to recognize it in Vader's technique during their duel.<ref name="TFUn" /> The Jedi Knight [[Jax Pavan]] also received Form II training at some point, applying some basic Makashi moves and tactics against [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]] in combat.<ref name="Street of Shadows" /> Makashi, like the other six forms, would eventually be rediscovered by the [[New Jedi Order]].<ref name="TJP" /><ref name="EGTTF" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:TCWDookuConceptArt.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Concept art of Dooku's lightsaber poses from [[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]]]
Makashi was first described in the [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization of ''Attack of the Clones'']], but while its specifications and history of the form were heavily expounded upon, it was never referenced by name. However, the [[Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat]] article in [[Star Wars Insider 62|''Star Wars Insider'' 62]], written by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]] and fencer Jack "Stelen" Bobo, identified it as Form II lightsaber combat. The proper name of the form, "Makashi", as well as its alternate titles as the "Contention Form" and the "Way of the Ysalamiri" would be specified in later sources.<ref name="Lightsabers" /><ref name="TJP" />

There are also Jedi and Sith who are theorized to practice Makashi based on descriptions and comments about their fighting techniques. Examples include [[Valenthyne Farfalla]], whose fighting style was described as elegant and clean, demonstrating perfect form,<ref name="DBRoT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref> and [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]], who was complimented by Dooku for keeping up his dueling skills and favoring the old ways.<ref name="Trackdown">[[Republic 72|''Republic'' 72]]</ref> Another likely practitioner of Makashi is [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]], based on statements in the official Databank and Dooku's labeling Bulq as a fencer.<ref name="Trackdown" /><ref name="SBD">{{DB|character|sorabulq|Bulq, Sora}}</ref> [[Xanatos]] is described in ''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Dark Rival]]'' to have fought with "economy and grace," indicating that he may have studied Makashi.<ref name="Dark Rival">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Dark Rival]]''</ref> In the epilogue of [[Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul|''Star Wars Episode I Journal: Darth Maul'']], Darth Sidious writes that [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] "is&mdash;was&mdash;an elegant fighter. Precise." Thus, Maul would've adopted a few tenets of Makashi into his fighting style.<ref name="E1J Maul">''[[Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul]]''</ref>

Makashi, along with the other lightsaber forms, appears in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' as part of moves and techniques employable by Jedi characters. This has not definitively been clarified to be canonical.<ref name="SonyCite-Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way">{{SonyCite|url=en_US/players/content.vm?id=66843&resource=features|text=Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way}}</ref>
